son: seer — they are (3rd pl.) · also son — perfect auxiliary of intransitives and passive auxiliary (todos son exidos 'have all gone out'; nombrados son; son derramadas 'are scattered')
las: el/la — the (fem. pl.); them (fem. object pronoun)
e: e — and (= modern y) · also aver — I have (1st sg. present, apocopated form of he, perfect auxiliary: Espeso e el oro, 'I have spent the gold') · also aver — 'I will', the future auxiliary in a split future (quitarvos e … darvos e de mano 'I will free you … I will let you go'; = vos quitaré, vos daré) · also the full verb 'I have' (el sabor que dend e 'the delight I have of it')
pareçen: pareçer — they look, appear (present 3rd pl.; non pareçen mal 'they look splendid'; = parecen)
los: el — the (masc. pl.); them (object pronoun) · also los que 'those who' (demonstrative use before a relative); los — him, them as object of consejar (commo los consejava 'as he advised them') · also los de 'those of' (con los de Castejón 'with the men of Castejón')
alvores: alvor — dawn, first light (masc., usually pl.; con los alvores 'at daybreak'; = albores, alba)
a: a — to, at · also aver — he/she has (3rd sg. present, h-less spelling of ha, as in el rey me a ayrado = el rey me ha airado) · personal a before a direct object (salvest a Jonás; a ti adoro); a + inf. 'to, about to' (tornólas a catar); a tan grand sabor 'with so great pleasure'; a ojo 'in plain sight' · also a — 'into' (sacar a çelada 'to lure into ambush'); 'at, in' (a la çaga 'at the rear'); 'against' (dar salto a la çaga); dative 'to' (a mí dedes); haber a + inf. 'have to' (lo han a far); a + noun of direction (adeliñava a la puerta 'made for the gate') · impersonal 'there is' (aver; es dia a de plazo 'there is (only) a day of the term', the most likely reading of a hard line); ha as auxiliary set after the participle (soñado a 'he has dreamt') · also 'on, at (a time)' (a tercer dia 'on the third day') · also a — 'has' before the participle, agreeing with the object (la lança a quebrada 'he has broken the lance'; a menester 'has need of'); a + dative of the person affected (a Minaya matáronle el cavallo 'they killed Minaya's horse') · a — 'as, for' (tóvoslo a grand fonta 'he took it as a great affront')
una: uno/una — one, a (fem.) · also a una — together, as one (adverbial; hivan a una compaña 'they went together'; a una grant ondrança 'together with great honor'; = juntos)
priessa: priessa — haste, bustle (a una priessa 'all in one bustle'; = prisa) · also a priessa — 'quickly, in haste' (adverbial; a priessa espoloneavan 'they spurred in haste')
atamores: atamor — drum (pl.; also atambor, from Arabic, with the article al- assimilated; ante roído de atamores 'at the din of the drums'; = tambores)
mio: mio — my (unstressed possessive; mio Çid 'my lord Cid')
çid: Çid — the Cid, 'lord' (Arabic sīdī 'my lord'; pronounced Tsid)
dixo: dezir — he/she said (strong preterite; x = sh-sound; = dijo)
es: seer — it is (present 3rd sg.) · also ser as perfect auxiliary of intransitives (exido es 'has gone out') and passive auxiliary (la tienda es cogida) · also es — that (apocopated esse = ese, demonstrative; en es alcaz 'in that pursuit', por es logar 'through that place')
su: su — his, her, its · also su — their (aquella su almofalla 'that host of theirs')
crebar: crebar — to break (infinitive; = quebrar); crebar albores 'dawn to break'
el: el — the (masc.) · also el — 'he who' before a relative (el qui quisiere, el que es sobre Fenares); el before a fem. noun beginning with a vowel (el espada = la espada; el algara = la algara) · also el de + place name 'he of, the one from' (mio Çid el de Bivar)
coraçón: coraçón — heart (= corazón) · also por coraçón 'willingly, heartily, with a will' (lo an por coraçón)
amas: amos — both (fem. pl., Latin ambas; las manos amas 'both hands'; = ambas)
del: de + el — of the (contraction) · also del standing for de + la before a feminine noun beginning with a vowel (del albergada = de la albergada) · also del — 'from, for, because of' (cause; del gozo 'from the joy'; del çerviçio 'for the service')
que: que — that, who, which; for · also por que — because, since (= porque) · por que — by which, whereby (por que más valdrá 'whereby he will be worth more') · also que — 'so that, lest' introducing purpose/result (que por miedo non dexen nada; por tal lo faze … que no lo ventasse nadi); after después/mientra 'after, while' (después que, mientra que) · also que — than, after a comparative (mas le vienen … que nos le van 'more come to him than leave him') · also que — what (indirect interrogative; dezir vos he que faze 'I shall tell you what he does'; = qué)
tal: tal — such; por tal 'for such a reason, for this purpose' (= tal)
la: el/la — the (fem.); her/it (object pronoun) · also la que 'the one that' (Çelfa la que dizen de Canal 'Çelfa, the one they call of the Canal')
campeador: Campeador — the Battler, the Champion (the Cid's epithet, from campo 'field of battle')
ayades: aver — you may have (present subjunctive 2nd pl., old -des ending; = hayáis)
ca: ca — for, because (Latin quia) · ca — perhaps 'but, whereas' (el uno es en paradiso, ca el otro non entró allá; the sense is uncertain)
todo: todo — all, every (de todo conducho, 'with every kind of provision')
pro: pro — worth, merit; de pro 'worthy, of good standing' · also pro — profit, advantage, benefit (grant pro les fazié 'he did them great good, was of great profit to them')
antes: antes — before; antes de 'before' · also antes que — 'before' (conjunction; antes quel prendan 'before they take him') · also antes — 'rather' (antes perderé el cuerpo 'rather shall I lose my body')
destos: de + estos — of these (contraction; en cada uno destos años 'in each one of these years'; = de estos)
si: si — if; si + subjunctive alone = 'if only …!' · si non — otherwise, if not (si non, do sopiéredes 'if not, wherever you learn'); si + future subjunctive 'if' (si nos falláredes 'if you find us') · also si — si'nulla = sin + nulla with -n assimilated before n- (si'nulla dubda 'without any fear' (or 'doubt'); = sin ningún miedo, sin ninguna duda)
ploguiere: plazer — (as long as) it may please (future subjunctive 3rd sg., strong; mientra ploguiere al Padre 'as long as it please the Father'; si vos ploguiere 'if it please you'; = pluguiere)
al: a + el — to the; al menos 'even the least' · also a + el standing for a + la before a feminine noun beginning with a vowel (al espada = a la espada) · also al — 'other thing, the rest' (neuter, Latin alius; de lo al non pienssan nada 'of anything else they think nothing'; distinct from a + el) · also a + el before an infinitive 'on, upon' (al exir de Salón 'on leaving the Jalón'; = al salir) · al 'the other thing, the rest' in al feredes adelant 'the rest you will do later'
abremos: aver — we shall have (future 1st pl., syncopated; = habremos)
ganar: ganar — to gain, earn · also 'to capture, take (a fortress)' (Alcoçer cueda ganar 'he expects to take Alcocer') · also ganar — to till, work the land (Pidal, like Old French gaignier; non se treven ganar 'they dare not work their fields'; = labrar)
aquellos: aquel — those (masc. pl. demonstrative; con aquellos que 'with those who'; = aquellos)
vos: vos — you (object pronoun, polite/plural) · also subject 'you' (vos, que por mí dexades 'you who leave for my sake'); dative 'to you' (dar vos quiero vuestra part) · also reflexive/ethic 'you (yourselves)' (id vos en algara 'go off on a raid'); dative with an impersonal sense (si cueta vos fore 'if need befall you')
delant: delant — ahead, in front (apocopated adverb; = delante)
veredes: ver — you will see (future 2nd pl., old -edes ending; = veréis)
desí: desí — from there, thence; thereupon (adverb, des + i 'there'; e desí arriba 'and from there upward'; = desde allí, después) · also desí — next, then in a series (desí a Molina 'next Molina')
an: aver — they have (3rd pl. present of aver = han) · perfect auxiliary (passados los an 'they have passed'; la missa acabada la an 'they have finished'); an por troçir 'there remain to pass'; an ... ha far 'they have to do, are to do' · also future auxiliary after an infinitive, the split future (ve[e]rme an 'they will see me'; = me verán)
don: don — don, lord (honorific title) · also don — gift (noun; en don 'as a gift') · also don — from where, whence (= donde, de onde; Castejón don abremos grand enpara 'Castejón, from which we shall have great protection') · 'whereof, with which' (Pidal 'de lo cual'; don yo sea pagado 'whereof I may be satisfied') · also don — when, where (= donde, of time; Don llegan los otros 'when the others come up')
jerome: Jerome — Jerónimo, the Cid's bishop of Valencia (Pidal restores Jero[me], 'don Jerome'; = Jerónimo)
han: aver — they have (present 3rd pl.; = han); after an infinitive, the auxiliary of a split future (seervos han = os serán) · also han a + inf. 'they have to, are bound to' (mandado de so señor todo lo han a far); 'they hold, possess' (que moros las han) · also perfect auxiliary 'have' with a participle agreeing with its object (la ganançia que han fecha 'the booty they have made')
en: en — in, into, on · en — of it, thence (= ende; por en avemos qué fablar 'of which we have to speak') · also en — 'as' (en paria 'as tribute'); en essora 'at that moment' · also en — 'among' (en todos los sos 'among all his men') · also en + infinitive 'in (doing)' (en levarlo adelant 'in carrying it forward'); en çinco días 'in five days'
santa: santo — Saint (fem.); Santa María, the cathedral of Burgos · santa — holy (adjective; santa Trinidad 'the Holy Trinity', santa María madre 'holy Mary, (thy) mother', the Virgin)
maría: María — Mary; Santa María, the cathedral of Burgos · also Santa María — Albarracín (Teruel), held by the Aben Razín (Pidal; por Santa María vos vayades passar)
fizo: fazer — he made, did, caused (strong preterite 3rd sg.; fizo posar 'he made (them) halt'; = hizo)
van: ir — they go (present 3rd pl.) · also ir + gerund 'keep going' (passando van 'they go on passing') · also ir + infinitive 'go to' (le van çercar 'they go to besiege him'; se van tornar 'they go back')
moros: moro — Moor (masc. pl.); a moros nin a cristianos, 'to any living soul' (merism)
de: de — of, from · also de — by (the agent with a passive participle; = por) · also de — 'by (night)' (de noch), partitive 'of, among' (quinze moros … de los que alcançava; pocas de gentes), 'as' (de ganançia 'as booty'), 'from outside' (de fuera), 'on the right' (de diestro) · also 'about, concerning' (de mí non digan mal 'let them not speak ill of me') · also de — 'as if in' (commo de arrancada 'as if in rout'); 'in the manner of' (de guisa 'in such a way'); 'of, among' (de bivos pocos 'of the living few'); nominalized infinitive (del prender 'of the taking') · also de — 'with' of manner (de fuertes coraçones 'with stout hearts'); 'on' (de pie 'on foot'); 'from' of side (della e della part 'from both sides'); de cabo 'anew' (de + cabo, 'again'); de suso de 'above'; seños … de seños colpes 'with one blow each' · also de — 'in respect of' after an adjective (sobejana de mala 'exceedingly bad'); 'with regard to, about' (me plaze de mio Çid 'I am pleased about the Cid'); 'from, at the hand of' (de señor non ha graçia 'he gets no favor from a lord'); 'from' of origin (de moros fo 'it came from Moors'); 'at' of manner (de vagar 'at leisure', de + the noun vagar) · also de’ — Pidal's de’llaño, read as del llaño 'of the plain' (the article's l run into the ll; a reading, not certain) · de + infinitive after an adjective (de ir somos guisados 'we are ready to go') · also de + infinitive after a verb: començar de 'to begin to' (compeçó de fablar 'he began to speak'), piénssanse de 'set about' (piénssanse de armar), aver de 'to have to' (lo que ha de far 'what he has to do') · also de — 'within' of a time limit (De aquestos quinze días, most likely 'within these fifteen days'; sense uncertain); de veluntad 'willingly'; de + superlative partitive (de los mejores guarnimientos 'of the best equipment')
marruecos: Marruecos — Morocco (rey de Marruecos 'the king of Morocco', i.e. the Almoravid ruler; = Marruecos)
cavalgan: cavalgar — they ride, mount (present 3rd pl.; = cabalgan)
por: por — through, along, by, for · purpose, 'in order to' (por el reyno quitar 'to quit the kingdom'); por + inf. 'yet to be done' (tres an por troçir 'three remain to pass'); 'for, on behalf of' (por mio Çid) · also por — 'out of, because of' (por miedo 'through fear'); 'for (that reason)' (por tal lo faze 'he does it for that reason'); 'by way of' (por Guadalfajara); por + noun 'for the sake of' ; por coraçón 'willingly' · also 'for (a price)' (por quanto serié conprada 'for how much it would be bought'); 'by means of' (por carta 'by writ'); 'through, thanks to' (por mí ganaredes 'through me you will gain') · also por — 'on, during (a time)' (por aquesta mañana 'this morning'); 'by way of, through' (por medio de la llaña 'through the middle of the plain') · also por — 'in' after fiar (yo fío por Dios 'I trust in God') · also por — 'to fetch, for' after enbiar/ir (enbiaré por ellas, irán por ellas 'I shall send for them', 'they will go for them'); por cuenta 'by count, in a count' · also por — as (por heredad 'as a possession')
huertas: huerta — irrigated garden land, orchard (fem. pl.; = huertas)
sines: sines — without (= sin, with added -es; sines dubdança 'without hesitation')
mesnadas: mesnada — household troop, band of followers (pl.; = mesnadas)
yentes: yente — people, folk (= gente; y- from Latin g-)
roy: Roy — Ruy, short for Rodrigo (Roy Díaz = Rodrigo Díaz, the Cid)
dan: dar — they give (present 3rd pl.; vagar non se dan 'they allow themselves no leisure'; = dan) · also dar — 'to pay (tribute)' (dan parias 'they pay tribute')
salto: salto — leap, jump · also dash, sally (dar salto 'to make a sortie'; non osa ninguno dar salto a la çaga 'none dares to dash at the rearguard')
mucho: mucho — much, greatly · also mucho — very, intensifying a predicate (mucho es mañana 'it is much too early, too soon') · also mas mucho — 'more' (mucho as a comparative = más: mas mucho fue provechosa 'was more profitable'; Pidal)
guisa: guisa — manner, fashion; a guisa de 'in the fashion of' · a vuestra guisa 'as you see fit, in your own way' (prended a vuestra guisa 'take as you please') · also de guisa que 'in such a way that' (de guisa irán por ellas que … 'in such a manner will they go for them that …'; = de modo que)
dellos: de + ellos — of them, from them (contraction)
conplidos: conplido — complete, full (past part. used as adjective, masc. pl.; todos foron conplidos 'all were complete, at full strength'; = cumplidos, completos; the exact sense is somewhat uncertain)
bien: bien — well · bien — good, benefit (noun; algún bien vos pueda far 'some good I may do you') · bien — very, quite, intensifying an adverb (bien çerca del agua 'very near the water')
fata: fata — until, as far as (variant of fasta; = hasta)
alcaz: alcaz — pursuit, chase (verbal noun of alcançar; en alcaz 'in pursuit'; modern alcance means 'reach', closest persecución)
avién: aver — they had (imperfect 3rd pl., perfect auxiliary forming the pluperfect; que y avién fallado 'that they had found there'; = habían)
piénssanse: pensar + se — they set about (present 3rd pl. + reflexive; piénssanse de adobar 'they set about getting ready'; = se ponen a)
tornar: tornar — to return; tornar palabra 'to answer a word' · also tornar — 'to give back' (tornar nos la ha doblada 'will give it back to us doubled'; infinitive + enclitic + ha, future); to turn (round), transitive (mandó tornar la seña 'he had the banner turned about')
álbar: Álbar — Álvar (personal name, Álbar Fáñez; = Álvar)
salvadórez: Salvadórez — patronymic 'son of Salvador' (modern cognate Salvadores)
preso: prender — taken (past part.; grand aver avemos preso 'we have taken great wealth'; = preso, prendido) · also so consejo preso ane 'they have taken their counsel, have resolved'
fincó: fincar — he planted, set firm (preterite; fincar los inojos 'to kneel') · also fincar — he stayed, remained (el Campeador fincó con su mesnada 'the Cid stayed with his troop'; = quedó)
tornados: tornar — turned back, returned (past part. masc. pl., agreeing with los 'them'; a los moros dentro los an tornados 'they have put the Moors back inside'; = vueltos, devueltos)
so: so/su — his, her, its (unstressed possessive sg.; so çervicio = su servicio); also seer — I am (1st sg. present; = soy; so ayrado, 'I am in [the king's] ira') · lo so — 'what is his, his own' (neuter article + possessive; lo so puede menguar 'what is his may dwindle') · also so — their (so consejo 'their counsel', so vino 'their wine'; = su)
él: él — he (stressed subject pronoun) · also él — 'him, it' after a preposition, of a thing (a él vino; en él fincaredes 'in it', i.e. in Castejón)
se: se — himself/herself/itself (reflexive pronoun) · also se — passive 'is, are' (cómmo se gana el pan 'how bread is earned'; = se, passive-reflexive)
lo: lo — him, it (object pronoun) · lo que perdedes 'that which you lose' (neuter antecedent of the relative) · also lo — neuter article 'what is' (lo to 'what is yours'); pleonastic 'it' (lo an, lo han a far; por tal lo faze 'for that reason he does it')
vío: veer — he saw (strong preterite of veer 'to see'; = vio, here two syllables ví-o)
quanto: quanto — as much as, whatever (= cuanto) · quanto ella mejor sabe 'as best she can' (quanto + comparative 'as much as') · also 'how much' (por quanto serié conprada 'for how much it would be bought'); 'as far/fast as' (quanto pueden andar) · tanto quanto 'as long as'; por quanto … ha 'for all that there is' (por quanto en el mundo ha)
oídme: oír + me — hear me (imperative 2nd pl. oíd + enclitic me; = oídme)
rastará: rastar — it will remain (future 3rd sg.; non rastará por al 'it shall not be otherwise', Pidal 'no quedará de otro modo'; = quedará)
bueno: bueno — good, fine, great (qué bueno es el gozo 'how great is the joy'; = bueno)
mejor: mejor — better, best (adverb; quanto ella mejor sabe 'as best she knows how'; = mejor)
cras: cras — tomorrow (adverb, Latin cras; cras a la mañana 'tomorrow morning'; modern uses mañana)
mañana: mañana — morning (a la mañana 'in the morning'; otro dia mañana 'next morning'; = mañana) · also mañana — early, soon (adverb/predicate; mucho es mañana 'it is too soon (to take back a man in disgrace after only three weeks)'; = pronto, temprano)
armados: armar — armed (past participle masc. pl.; vídolos venir armados 'he saw them come armed'; = armados)
seades: seer — you may be (present subjunctive 2nd pl., old -ades ending; = seáis)
do: do — where, as (relative adverb, Latin de ubi; = donde) · also do — wherever, whenever (generalizing, with subjunctive: do yo vos enbiás 'wherever I might send you'; the exact sense is uncertain) · also dar — I give (present 1st sg.; d'aquí vos do mi graçia 'from here I give you my favor'; = doy)
nos: nos — we (subject pronoun; = nosotros) · also nos — us, to us (object pronoun; atorgar nos hedes 'you will grant us') · also reflexive 'ourselves' (nos partimos 'we part'); dative (la missa nos dirá 'will say for us') · also nos' — non + se (aun nos' van del campo 'they are still not leaving the field'; the apostrophe marks the elision) · also nos — non + se, written without apostrophe (nin amigo a amigo nos pueden consolar 'nor can friend console friend'; mas le vienen … que nos le van 'more come to him than leave him', the no redundant after the comparison)
ha: aver — he has (3rd sg. present; = ha) · ha — to (a with h-, aver a + inf. 'will, must': lo an todos ha far 'all are to do it'); aver — has, possesses (las fijas que ha 'the daughters she has') · also ha — future ending after infinitive + clitics, the split future (tornar nos la ha 'he will give it back to us'; = nos la tornará) · also ha — there is, there are (impersonal; dos señas ha cabdales 'there are two chief banners'; = hay) · also ha — perfect auxiliary 'has' before the participle (ha vendido 'has sold'; fechos los ha ricos 'has made them rich') · also 'has, gets' (de señor non ha graçia 'he has no favor from a lord') · also ha de + inf. 'is to' (que los ha de aguardar 'who is to attend them'; aver de + infinitive, = ha de)
ir: ir — to go (infinitive; = ir) · ir + gerund in a split future (ir nos hemos pagando 'we shall go on paying ourselves'; = nos iremos pagando)
hemos: aver — we will/shall (1st pl. future auxiliary; restored by Pidal in the split future dar gelos [hemos] = se los daremos)
nombre: nombre — name; por nombre 'by name, called' (= nombre)
d: de — of, with (elided form of de before a vowel, d'arena = de arena) · de — from (unos d'otros 'one from another')
santi: santi — saint (old form before a saint's name, from Latin sancti as in Sancti Iacobi, which survives fused in Santiago; santi Yagüe 'Saint James'; = santo, san)
yague: Yague — James (Latin Iacobus; santi Yague 'Saint James', the apostle, Spain's patron; = Santiago)
más: más — more; e más 'and moreover' · non más 'no more, nothing more'; por que más valdrá 'whereby he will be worth more'
vale: valer — it is worth (present 3rd sg.; que más vale de mill marcos 'which is worth more than a thousand marks'; = vale) · also va + le — 'it goes on (…ing) for him' (ir + gerund with enclitic le: Yal creçe la barba e vale allongando 'and it goes on lengthening for him'; = se le va alargando)
ellos: ellos — they, them (stressed 3rd pl. masc. pronoun)
essora: essora — then, at that moment (ess' + ora; en essora 'at that moment'; = entonces)
dixieron: dezir — they said (strong preterite 3rd pl., x = sh-sound; así commo a mí dixieron 'as they told me'; = dijeron)
voluntad: voluntad — will, willingness; de voluntad e de grado, a doubled formula, 'willingly and gladly' · God's will (commo fo tu voluntad 'as was your will'); de toda voluntad 'with all one's heart' · also de buena voluntad 'gladly, willingly' (the formula of assent); a toda su voluntad 'wholly to his satisfaction, at his will'
fablava: fablar — he was speaking (imperfect 3rd sg.; = hablaba)
minaya: Minaya — the title by which the Cid's kinsman Álvar Fáñez is called, usually explained as mi + anaya 'my brother'
quiso: querer — he wished (strong preterite 3rd sg.; non quiso 'he did not want'; = quiso)
detardar: detardar — to delay, put off (infinitive; non lo quiso detardar 'he would not put it off'; = tardar, demorar)
esso: esso — that (neuter demonstrative; esso con esto 'that together with this'; = eso)
mandedes: mandar — you order (present subjunctive 2nd pl., command; = mandéis)
huebos: huebos — need (Latin opus); huebos (me) ser/aver = 'to have need (of)'
lidiar: lidiar — to fight (infinitive; = lidiar, closest luchar)
fóredes: seer — (when) you shall be (future subjunctive 2nd pl. of ser, Pidal's [ó]; quando fóredes yantado 'when you have dined'; = fuereis)
ferir: ferir — to strike, attack (infinitive; vayámoslos ferir 'let us go and strike them'; = herir)
otra: otro — other (fem. sg.; del otra part 'on the other side', with el before a vowel-initial feminine noun, = de la otra parte)
part: part — share, portion (noun; = parte) · also part — side (del otra part 'on the other side'; = parte)
o: o — or; also ó — where (interrogative, Latin ubi; ¿O sodes…? 'Where are you…?') · also o — where (relative adverb; o dizen Castejón 'which they call Castejón'; o el Campeador estava 'where the Campeador was'; = donde) · correlative 'either … or' (o me dexaredes … o … levaredes 'either you will leave me … or you will take away')
dios: Dios — God · also Dios! — interjection of wonder (Dios, cómmo se alabavan! 'God, how they boasted!')
valdrá: valer — he will be worth, will count for (future 3rd sg.; = valdrá)
buena: bueno — good (fem.); en buen(a) '(born/girded) in a good hour' — the poem's honorific formula
salido: salir — gone out, exiled (past part., used as a noun; el salido de Castiella 'the one banished from Castile'; = salido)
noch: noche — night (apocopated form of noche; cf. anoch)
detardan: detardar — they delay (present 3rd pl.; cf. detardava)
cristianas: cristiano — Christian (fem. pl.; las yentes cristianas = 'everyone')
mediados: mediado — middle, half-way through (past participle used as adjective; los mediados gallos 'the mid-cockcrow'; = mediados)
les: les — to them · also les — 'from them', dative of removal or injury (les tollió el pan 'took the bread from them'; viédales exir 'forbids them to go out')
dicha: dezir — said (past participle fem.; la missa dicha 'mass having been said'; = dicha)
dava: dar — he gave (imperfect) · also dar se — 'to give itself up, surrender' (Alcoçer non se le dava 'Alcocer did not surrender to him')
aquí: aquí — here; d'aquí 'from here' · also 'then, at this point' (aquí dixo el comde 'then the count said')
le: le — to him, him (dative pronoun) · also le — him, as direct object (leísmo; si ellos le prenden 'if they take him'); dative (non se le dava 'did not surrender to him') · also le — dative of separation, 'from him' (que nos le parte de so braço 'who does not leave his side'); dative 'for him' (ques le non spidiés 'who does not take leave of him')
abrá: aver — he will have (future 3rd sg., b for v; de lo nuestro abrá 'he will have of ours'; = habrá)
rodrigo: Rodrigo — Rodrigo, the Cid's given name (= Rodrigo)
çinxiestes: çeñir — you girded (strong preterite 2nd pl. of çeñir; Latin cinxistis)
aquesta: aquesta — this (fem. sg., reinforced demonstrative; = esta, archaic aquesta)
aya: aver — I may have (present subjunctive 1st sg.; = haya) · also aya — he may have (present subjunctive 3rd sg., same form as 1st; de Dios aya su graçia 'may he have God's grace', optative; = haya)
sean: seer — let them be (present subjunctive 3rd pl., jussive; todos sean contados 'let them all be counted'; = sean)
